title: The Lost Maximum
concept: Finding the maximum value in an array
description: Deep in Array Forest, an ancient monolith holds a series of numbered stones. Find the stone bearing the maximum value to unlock the path forward.
learning_objective: Master single-pass linear traversal, maintaining running maximum state, and loop invariant verification.
hints: What are you being asked to find?
Think about what you can remember while scanning the array.
Keep track of the largest value seen so far.

stages.name: Understand the Goal
stages.prompt: What is the primary objective and return value of this problem?
options: Find and return the largest numerical element present in the array
Sort the entire array in ascending order
Count how many even numbers exist in the array
Return the index of the first element
hints: Review the problem objective: what value needs to be retrieved from the stones?
Focus on the word 'maximum' — it's about the value, not the array ordering.
stages.explanation: The problem specifically asks to identify the single largest number in the array.

stages.name: Identify the Pattern
stages.prompt: Which algorithmic pattern is best suited to find the maximum in an unsorted array of unknown size?
options: Binary search on the unsorted array
Single-pass linear traversal tracking the largest element seen so far
Breadth-first graph traversal
Recursive backtracking generating all permutations
hints: Since the array is unsorted, any element could be the maximum.
Every element must be inspected at least once in O(N) time.
stages.explanation: A single linear pass O(N) tracking `current_max` is the optimal approach for an unsorted array.

stages.name: Decompose into Steps
stages.prompt: What is the correct logical sequence of steps to decompose this algorithm?
options: 1. Initialize max to arr[0] -> 2. Loop i from 1 to N-1 -> 3. If arr[i] > max, update max -> 4. Return max
1. Sort array descending -> 2. Sum elements -> 3. Return average
1. Return arr[0] immediately without checking other elements
1. Iterate backwards -> 2. If element < max, terminate loop immediately
hints: You must establish a baseline running maximum before iterating.
Each step compares the next element with the current champion.
stages.explanation: Setting the baseline to the first element and updating whenever a strictly larger element appears is the standard decomposition.

stages.name: Predict Execution
stages.prompt: Given `arr = [3, 7, 2, 9, 5]` and `current_max` initialized to 3, how many times will `current_max` be updated during the loop?
options: 1 time
2 times (when encountering 7 and 9)
4 times
0 times
hints: Test each stone sequentially: 7 > 3 (update?), 2 > 7 (update?), 9 > 7 (update?), 5 > 9 (update?).
Count only when the 'if' condition evaluates to True.
stages.explanation: The maximum updates at element 7 (7 > 3) and element 9 (9 > 7). Element 2 and 5 do not trigger updates. Total updates = 2.

stages.name: Dry Run State Tracing
stages.prompt: Trace the variable state: At index `i = 3` (inspecting element 9), what is `current_max` BEFORE and AFTER that step?
options: Before: 7, After: 9
Before: 3, After: 7
Before: 9, After: 9
Before: 2, After: 5
hints: What was the value of current_max after index 2 (element 2 was evaluated)?
What happens when 9 is compared with 7?

stages.name: Solve & Code Pattern
stages.prompt: Select or provide the core assignment statement executed inside the loop when a larger element is found:
stages.code_snippet:
for num in nums[1:]:
    # Core update logic goes here
options: if num > max_val: max_val = num
if num < max_val: max_val = num
max_val += num
num = max_val
hints: The condition must verify that the inspected number is strictly greater than the current maximum.
The assignment must assign the new number into the maximum variable.
stages.explanation: The fundamental update logic is `if num > max_val: max_val = num`.

stages.name: Explain Complexity & Trade-offs
stages.prompt: Explain why this linear scan algorithm achieves O(N) time and O(1) space complexity:
options: It visits each of the N elements exactly once in a single pass, and only uses a single tracking variable `current_max`.
It allocates a new array of size N at each loop step, requiring exponential time.
It sorts the array in-place, which is always guaranteed O(N) in all languages.
The time complexity is O(N^2) because of hidden pointer dereferencing in arrays.
hints: Consider how many times the loop visits each array element.
Consider how much auxiliary memory is allocated besides the input array.
stages.explanation: Single traversal of N items requires O(N) operations. Only 1 extra variable `current_max` is maintained, which takes O(1) auxiliary space.

title: The Step-by-Step Tracker
description: Trace variable pointers across complex nested array traversals.
learning_objective: Build intuition for pointer state tracking and dry running loops.
hints: Focus on how variables change after each iteration.

title: Divide and Conquer Roots
description: Decompose complex array partitioning into clean sub-problems.
learning_objective: Learn to break array problems into independent modular steps.
hints: Break into base cases first.

title: The Riddle of the Constraints
description: Master constraint comprehension and edge cases in array algorithms.
learning_objective: Identify corner cases such as empty arrays, negative values, and single elements.
hints: What happens if all numbers are negative?
